observations.text: SP, due to an in flight planning technique that did not account for the fuel remaining at the working area, did not adjust the mission profile to the time and fuel constraints, with the result that the formation was flown 400 feet outside the assigned block and 25 knots off the planned airspeed and the IP had to direct the sequence of the remaining maneuvers. Formation consistency was restored only after the IP passed the required instructions to No2. Further practice in profile and fuel management as leader is required.

SP, due to mission-completion bias in pressing on past the briefed decision point, did not adjust the mission profile when the conditions in the assigned area deteriorated and did not pass the required breakout instruction to the wingman. The formation was flown 450 feet below the assigned block and 12 degrees off the briefed exit heading, with the result that the IP took the A/C and executed the repositioning. Recognition of the briefed decision points is required before the next formation sortie.

SP completed the in flight planning within the standards required for the Training Section, adjusting the maneuver sequence and informing the wingman after the IP's verbal prompts. Deviations reached 300 feet in altitude and 10 degrees on the exit heading before being recognized and corrected, with delay. Marginal performance for the block - earlier assessment of the fuel and time constraints and more timely instructions to No2 are expected to improve.

SP planned the profile in flight taking into account the meteorological conditions, the fuel state and the assigned lateral and vertical limits, and passed the required instructions to the wingman by radio without IP prompting. Minor deviations of 180 feet in altitude and 14 knots in airspeed during the change of the maneuver sequence were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP adjusted the mission profile to the fuel and time constraints accurately and rapidly, monitored the position of No2 throughout and kept the formation consistent through the change of sequence. Effect on the flight controls was smooth and progressive, and deviations remained within 90 feet in altitude, 6 knots in airspeed and 3 degrees on the exit heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP conducted the in flight planning to a standard above the desired level, sequencing the maneuvers so as to take advantage of the allocated fuel in the best way while keeping No2 clear of the sun and inside the assigned area. The formation remained flexible and consistent, the wingman was informed of every major flight data change before it was applied, and deviations were negligible at 40 feet in altitude, 3 knots in airspeed and 1 degree on the exit heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an energy conservation technique that did not preserve airspeed between the maneuvers, did not sequence the profile so as to keep the formation inside the assigned vertical limits, with the result of deviations of 30 knots in airspeed and 380 feet in altitude. The wingman was left without instructions during the repositioning and the IP had to execute part of the change of profile. The task was not completed without assistance.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and A/C control attempted simultaneously, did not check the position of No2 while re-planning the maneuver sequence. The exit heading was missed by 18 degrees and the altitude by 350 feet, with the result that the IP directed the breakout and re-established the formation. Shedding of secondary tasks when the workload increases requires further work.

SP, due to an incomplete assessment of the fuel remaining against the briefed profile, did not shorten the maneuver sequence at the point the fuel state required it, with the result of a 300 feet deviation from the assigned block and a 20 knots deviation in airspeed. The profile was adjusted and the wingman informed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a briefed decision point that was passed without any decision being made, did not re-plan the profile when the allocated working time in the area expired. The formation was taken out 10 degrees off the briefed exit heading and 20 knots below the planned airspeed. The sequence was corrected and No2 informed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of the deviation.

SP performed the in flight planning within the desired standards, adjusting the maneuver sequence to the fuel state and passing the required calls to the wingman without IP's intervention. Deviations of 230 feet in altitude and 15 knots in airspeed occurred twice during the changes of profile and were self-corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier anticipation of the energy required for the next maneuver is expected to improve formation consistency.

SP adjusted the mission profile accurately and rapidly to the meteorological conditions and the allocated fuel, kept the formation consistent and remained predictable to No2 throughout the sequence. Deviations did not exceed 120 feet in altitude, 7 knots in airspeed and 4 degrees on the exit heading, and every major flight data change was passed to the wingman before it was applied. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the profile in flight with exceptional accuracy, using the allocated fuel to complete the full maneuver sequence inside the assigned lateral and vertical limits and positioning No2 clear of the sun at every turn. Effect on the flight controls was smooth and progressive, the wingman held his position without correction through each change of profile, and deviations remained negligible at 50 feet in altitude, 4 knots in airspeed and 2 degrees on the exit heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a planning technique based on the briefed sequence alone, without reference to the actual fuel and time remaining, did not adjust the profile when the working area was reassigned, with the result that the formation exceeded the assigned block by 420 feet and the exit heading by 15 degrees. The required instructions were not provided to No2 and the IP had to take the A/C to re-establish the formation.

SP, due to rigid adherence to the briefed sequence after the conditions had changed, did not re-plan the maneuver order when the cloud base dropped below the working altitude. The formation was flown 350 feet outside the assigned vertical limits and 25 knots below the planned airspeed, and the breakout required by the manuals was not initiated. The IP directed the breakout and executed part of the recovery of the formation.

SP, due to an imprecise cross-check of the fuel state against the remaining profile, did not re-sequence the maneuvers in time to complete the sortie within the allocated fuel, with the result of a 300 feet deviation from the assigned altitude and a 10 degrees deviation on the exit heading. The profile was corrected and the wingman informed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with delayed recognition of the deviation.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the fuel state during the working phase of the sortie, did not adjust the mission profile to the time constraints and did not provide the wingman with the required instructions for the change of sequence. Airspeed reached 20 knots below the planned figure and altitude 300 feet from the assigned block. The deviations were recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts.

SP, due to a maneuver entry flown without pre-setting the energy required for the next segment, did not keep the change of profile as smooth as the formation required, with the result of a 200 feet deviation in altitude and a 7 degrees deviation on the exit heading. No2 held his position throughout, and the deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without IP's intervention.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, delayed the call informing the wingman of the change in the maneuver sequence. Airspeed varied by 16 knots and altitude by 240 feet before the formation was returned to the briefed profile. The error was self-corrected in a timely manner and the formation remained consistent, without IP's intervention.

SP performed the in flight planning to the desired standard, adjusting the profile to the meteorological conditions and the fuel available and keeping the formation consistent inside the assigned area. Deviations remained within 140 feet in altitude and 9 knots in airspeed, but on two occasions the instruction to No2 for the change of sequence was passed close to the maneuver entry. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier notification of the wingman for upcoming major flight data changes is expected to improve.

SP planned the profile in flight with exceptional accuracy, adjusting the maneuver sequence to the weather, the fuel and the assigned lateral and vertical limits without any prompting, and checking the position of No2 at any time. The formation remained flexible and consistent, every major flight data change was passed by visual signals or radio before it was applied, and deviations were negligible at 40 feet in altitude, 3 knots in airspeed and 1 degree on the exit heading. Above end of block MIF achieved.
